 PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATION – 5 MINUTES):

Citizens wishing to address the Commission on any matter which is within the subject matter jurisdiction
of the Planning Commission not on the Agenda may do so at this time. Please note that while the
Planning Commission values your comments, pursuant to the Brown Act, the Planning Commission cannot
take action unless the matter appears as an item on a forthcoming agenda.

COMMISSION COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS):

Each Commissioner at his/her discretion may address the Commission and public on matters of general
information and/or concern, including announcements and future agenda items.

ADJOURNMENT:

The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Alhambra Planning Commission will be held on Monday,
March 2, 2020, at 7:00 p.m., in Alhambra City Hall Council Chambers, 111 South First Street, Alhambra,
California.

  NOTICE:

AGENDA ITEMS: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed on
this agenda are on file in the offices of the Community Development Department in City Hall, located at
111 South First Street, Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours,
Monday through Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the Planning
Commission meeting agenda and staff report packet, please visit the City’s website at
www.cityofalhambra.org and you will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the
subscription service. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items
for regular meetings of the Alhambra Planning Commission that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to
that meeting, will be made available for public inspection at the Community Development Department.
Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact the Community Development Director either in person at the
Department offices, or by telephone at (626) 570-5034 during regular office hours.

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT: If you require special assistance to participate in the Planning
Commission meeting (including assisted listening devices) please contact the Community Development
Department at (626) 570-5034. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City
to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

TRANSLATION SERVICES REQUESTS: If you require translation services in order to participate in a
meeting please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 570-5090. All requests for translation services
shall be made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Planning Commission meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Planning Commission meeting, staff will try to
accommodate the request if possible.

APPEALS: Any person wishing to appeal any decision of the Planning Commission to the City Council may
do so by filing an appeal in writing along with the appropriate appeal fee to the Community Development
Department in City Hall within 10 calendar days of the Planning Commission decision. The appeal period

  3
 for items on this agenda expires at the close of business on March 2, 2020.

  Meeting Rules and Regulation

Section 2.24.060 of the Alhambra Municipal Code provides for the Planning Commission to establish and
enforce its own rules and regulations for its meetings. The Planning Commission uses those rules and
regulations established by the Municipal Code and implemented for use by the City Council.

Addressing the Commission: Any person wishing to address the Commission during the meeting must complete
a Speaker Request Card and submit it to the Secretary.

When called upon by the President, please step to the podium. Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the
President may either extend or reduce the maximum time to such period of time as the Commission may
determine.

All remarks shall be addressed to the Commission as a body and not to any member thereof. No person, other
than the Commission and the person having the floor, shall be permitted to enter into any discussion, either
directly or through a member of the Commission, without the permission of the President. No question shall be
asked a Commissioner except through the President.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Commission who refuses to stop speaking after his/her time
has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the progress of the
Planning Commission meeting who, after a request by the President, refuses to cease such behavior may be
removed from the City Council chambers upon direction of the President.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, may be Sergeant-at-Arms of the Commission
meetings. If present, the Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the President for
the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Commission meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City officials or their designees, shall be permitted
within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the express consent of the Commission.

PROPOSAL
The applicant is requesting the approval of a Commercial Planned Development Permit to establish
a used auto sales business on a property that has been vacant for more than six (6) months on a
property of approximately 6,900 square feet located in the VSP (Valley Boulevard Corridor
Specific Plan) zone.

  CP 19-16
  Page 1 of 18
 LOCATION
The site is located on the northern side of Valley Boulevard, on the northwest corner of Valley
Boulevard and Date Avenue. The subject property is located in the VSP (Valley Boulevard
Corridor Specific Plan) zone and is surrounded by a variety of uses that include several restaurants,
offices including dental and professional, automobile services, and automobile sales. The subject
property is developed with a one-story, 1,042 square foot commercial building with an attached
carport and five (5) on-site parking spaces located at the rear of the property.

ANALYSIS
The applicant is requesting the approval of a Commercial Planned Development Permit to establish
a used auto sales business on a property that has been vacant for more than six (6) months. In
accordance with AMC Section 23.62.020(B)(4), a Planned Development Permit shall be required
for commercially zoned properties for any application for certificate of occupancy for the use of a
building which has been vacant for more than six (6) months. Given that the property has been
vacant for more than six (6) consecutive months, a Planned Development Permit is required to
reoccupy the property, including reinstating a used automobile dealership consistent with an
approved Conditional Use Permit (CU-07-22).
In accordance with the Valley Boulevard Corridor Specific Plan (VSP), the current land use
designation for the subject property is identified as Residential Specific Plan (RSP) and Retail
Commercial (RC). Section 23.37.030 of the Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC) stipulates that
those uses conditionally permitted in the Commercial Planned Development (CPD) zone are
conditionally permitted in the VSP-RC zone, which the subject property is currently located. The
subject property currently has an approved Conditional Use Permit (CU-07-22) for the use of a
used auto sales business that was approved on September 4, 2007. In May of 2011, a new certificate
of occupancy was submitted to the City to establish a tint shop use. However, on April of 2019,
the tint shop business relocated to a different location within the City. Since then the property has
remained vacant, surpassing the six (6) month period.
The subject property has an existing 1,042 square foot building that will serve as the dealership
office housing two desk areas, a storage room, and a restroom. There will be no alterations or
interior improvements to the building or carport, however, the applicant will be removing an
unpermitted partition wall located inside the commercial building.
The proposed auto dealership will employ two (2) staff members and will operate 7 days a week,
Monday thru Sunday from 9:00am to 7:00pm.
The subject property currently provides five (5) on-site parking spaces at the rear of the property.
In accordance with AMC Section 23.52.040, one parking space shall be required for every 500
square feet within a building and one space for every 1,000 square feet of outdoor display and
storage area. In addition to the existing 1,042 square foot building, there is also an existing 1,320
square foot carport/display area adjacent to the east side of the building facing Valley Boulevard
and Date Avenue that will used as a display area. The proposed use will require a total of five (5)
parking spaces. The current parking meets code requirements as there will be five parking spaces
for employees and customers. The applicant will install a 30-inch deep landscape planter at the
perimeter of the property along the Valley Boulevard and Date Avenue frontages. The applicant
will not alter or modify the building.

  CP 19-16

 ENVIRONMENTAL STATUS
This application is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act, Section
15301, Existing Facilities, Class 1 consisting of no expansion of use beyond the existing
commercial structure. The project will not consist of any interior alterations including interior
partitions, plumbing, and electrical conveyances, therefore, it is exempt from CEQA.

PUBLIC NOTICE
On February 4, 2020, a Notice of Public Hearing was sent to 91 property owners of properties
within a 300-foot radius of the project site. A legal notice advertising the public hearing was placed
in the Pasadena Star News on February 7, 2020. A notice was also posted on the property on
January 30, 2020. No comments have been received from any of the parties notified in the area as
of the date this report was finalized.

CONCLUSION
The Applicant is requesting to establish a used auto sales business on a property that is zoned VSP-
RC. The subject property is suitable for a used auto dealership and meets the required parking
spaces. Although the building has been used in the past years as a tint shop business, the proposed
business will not require a new Conditional Use Permit as there is an approved Conditional Use
Permit (CU-07-22) for a used auto sales business. In accordance with AMC Section
23.62.020(B)(4), a Planned Development Permit is required as the property has been vacant for
more than six (6) months. The proposed used auto dealership will contribute to the mixture of uses
and businesses that will improve the economic base for the City. Therefore, staff recommends
approval of this project.

STAFF RECOMMENDED ACTION
Staff recommends Planning Commission to:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 20-8, approving Commercial Planned Development Permit CP-19-
  16, to establish a used auto sales business on a property that has been vacant for more than
  six (6) months on a property of approximately 6,900 square feet located in the VSP (Valley

  (Exhibit A) for the property located at 2207 West Valley Boulevard in the City of
  Alhambra.

  2. Direct staff to file and post a Notice of Exemption in accordance with Section 15062 of the

ANALYSIS
The applicant is requesting approval of a Planned Development Permit and a parking Variance for
230 and 234 W Main Street to establish an entitlement for a general retail and office use within an
existing two-story commercial building. A Planned Development Permit is required pursuant to
Alhambra Municipal Code Section 23.62.020(B)(3) for the use of a building which has been vacant
for more than six (6) months. Although both units have been vacant for more than six (6) months,
it is the intent of the property owner to entitle the building to attract two (2) new tenants to occupy
the vacant building.
The Alhambra Municipal Code’s parking requirements are based on uses and their floor areas, and
staff has determined that the property is currently under-parked. The current building occupies
more than 90% of the property with no additional space for parking, which makes it impossible
for any type of use that may occupy the building. As such the applicant is requesting a Variance
for a reduction in the parking requirements to be able to accommodate future business office and
retail uses. General business office uses and retail uses have the same parking standard requiring
one (1) parking space per 250 square feet of floor area. The “Parking Requirements” table below
shows the floor area sizes for each of the two units and the required parking at 1 space per 250
square feet:

 SECTION 4. VARIANCE FINDINGS. Based on the forgoing facts and findings (Section 23.68.060 of

follows:

A.  There are special circumstances or exceptional characteristics applicable to the property involved,
  including size, shape, topography, location or surroundings, such that strict application of the
  zoning ordinance deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under the identical zoning classification:

  The subject property was developed in 1921 with the building occupying over 90% of the lot while
  providing no on-site parking spaces. Pursuant to the Alhambra Municipal Code, general retail and
  business office uses for the subject building’s area would require a total 36 off-street parking spaces,
  which the subject property is unable to provide since the lot is built-out. Alhambra Municipal Code
  Section 23.52.060(F) allows the Planning Commission to count City-owned public parking facilities
  within 400 feet of a use towards waiving all or part of a development’s on-site parking requirements.
  There are three (3) City-owned public parking facilities within 400 feet of the subject site which
  will provide a total of 108 parking spaces. They are generally located to the south, north, and east
  of the subject site accessible from Third and Second Streets. The subject property abuts a City-
  owned public parking lot containing 33 parking spaces, is located approximately 115 feet of a Semi-
  Public parking garage containing 25 public spaces in the Casita de Zen development, and is also
  approximately within 290 feet of a City-owned public parking lot containing 50 parking spaces.

  Since a total of 108 public parking spaces are available within a 400-foot radius of the site, the
  Planning Commission finds that there will be adequate parking spaces to accommodate future office
  and commercial retail uses.

B.  The granting of such variance will not be detrimental to the public interest, safety, health or welfare,
  and will not be detrimental or injurious to the property or improvements in the vicinity and zone in
  which the property is located:

  There is a total of 108 public parking spaces provided within a 400-foot radius of the subject site by
  means of parking garages and surface lots located generally to the west of the subject site accessible
  from Second Street and Third Street. The proposed entitlements will facilitate the establishment of
  future business office and commercial retail uses that will not increase or expand the area or cause
  an increased in parking demand. There are adequate public parking opportunities within the
  immediate vicinity that will be adequate to accommodate future uses. The granting of this variance
  will not be detrimental to property or improvements in the vicinity and zone since patrons will be
  able to park in a nearby parking garage and safely access the proposed business.

C.  The granting of such variance will not be contrary to or in conflict with the general purposes and
  intent of the Zoning Ordinance, nor to the goals and programs of the General Plan:

  The granting of the Variance will not be contrary to or in conflict with the general purposes and
  intent of the Zoning Ordinance nor to the goals and programs of the General Plan. The building

PROPOSAL
This is a request for a Planned Development Permit and a Variance to allow a food service
establishment to occupy the existing 2,240 square foot building that was previously a vocational
use on an approximate land area of 3,450 square feet located in the CBD (Central Business District)
zone and DRD (Downtown Revitalization Overlay District). The Variance is requested for a
reduction in the number of required on-site parking spaces.

 LOCATION
The site is located on the south side of Main Street, between South Third Street and South Second
Street. The site is also located in the Downtown Revitalization District and is surrounded by
commercial and mixed-use buildings with a variety of uses including restaurants, retail stores,
professional offices, and technical and professional schools. In addition to the frontage along Main
Street, the subject property and building is also accessible from an alley located at the rear.

ANALYSIS
The applicant is requesting approval of a Planned Development Permit and a Variance to allow a
food service establishment to occupy the existing 2,240 square foot commercial space that was last
occupied by Pedrini School of Music and Guitar Lessons with Angelo. A Planned Development
Permit is required pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC) Section 23.62.020(B)(4) since
the proposed use intensifies the parking from a 1:125 ratio (Vocational use) to a 1:120 ratio (Food
and Beverage Establishment use). The proposed use will increase the required number of parking
by one (1) space. Permitting a food service establishment use will allow the applicant to provide a
move-in ready space for uses that are defined by the Municipal Code as a food service
establishment. The applicant’s request to entitle a food service establishment will make the
commercial space more attractive and marketable for future tenants. These uses may include but
are not limited to restaurants, bakeries, cafes, coffee shops, fast food, fast casuals, or other similar
uses. The applicant will not be permitted to sell alcoholic beverages as part of this application. If
the applicant in the future wishes to sell alcoholic beverages, they will need to apply for a
Conditional Use Permit and seek approval from the Planning Commission in accordance with
AMC Section 23.28.030(Z). No outdoor dining is proposed as part of this application, however, if
the applicant would like to have outdoor dining in the future, they will need to apply for a
Conditional Use Permit and seek approval from the Planning Commission in accordance with
AMC Section 23.28.030(U).

Parking Variance
The Alhambra Municipal Code’s parking requirements are based on uses and their floor areas. As
presented in the parking table below, under the AMC §23.52: [Off-Street Parking and Loading
Standards], a food service establishment comprised of 2,240 square feet shall provide a minimum
of 19 parking spaces at a 1:120 ratio, while the previous use required a minimum of 18 parking
spaces. Although the property in the past has had on-site parking, the layout of those spaces do not
adhere to the Parking Design Standards pursuant to Alhambra Municipal Code (AMC) Section
23.52.070. Due to the narrow width of the lot (25 feet wide), the proposed project will not be able
to provide the minimum number of parking spaces as required by the Zoning Ordinance. Only one
(1) ADA parking space will be provided on-site which vehicular access will be provided via a
single drive entrance from the alley at the rear of the property as required by the Building Code.

Under the Zoning Ordinance, businesses may be able to obtain a Parking Variance if the property
is within 400 feet of a City-owned public parking lot. There are a total of 108 public parking spaces
within 400 feet of the project site generally to the south, north, and east of the subject site accessible
from 3rd and 2nd Streets. The subject property abuts a City-owned public parking lot containing 33
parking spaces, is located approximately 115 feet of a Semi-Public parking garage containing 25
public spaces in the Casita de Zen development, and is also approximately within 290 feet of a
City-owned public parking lot containing 50 parking spaces. It is customary for cities to provide
parking for businesses in a Downtown District as they tend to not have room to accommodate
parking due to past transportation practices prior to the automobile. Therefore, a Parking Variance
is recommended to negate the deficient minimum parking required for a food service establishment
pursuant to AMC Section 23.52.060(F) [Reduction of Requirements].

CONCLUSION
The proposed use will change the parking standards from a 1:125 ratio (vocational use) to a 1:120
ratio (food service establishment use), increasing the overall number of required parking spaces
by one (1). However, a Parking Variance will allow the applicant to utilize the public parking
facilities pursuant to AMC Section 23.52.060(F) [Reduction of Requirements]. The applicant’s
request to entitle a food service establishment will make the commercial space more attractive and
marketable for future tenants. Therefore, staff recommends approval of this project.

A.  There are special circumstances or exceptional characteristics applicable to the property involved,
